principles.definition: Inclusive design creates workspaces that are accessible and functional for people of all abilities, ages, body types, and working styles without requiring special adaptation
principles.businessCase: Inclusive workspaces reduce employer liability, improve retention of staff with disabilities, and create more ergonomic outcomes for all staff
principles.legalObligation: Disability Discrimination Act 1992 — reasonable adjustments required in workplaces. AS 1428 compliance expected in new fitouts.

workstationInclusion.heightAdjustable: Sit-stand desks are the single most inclusive furniture investment — they accommodate wheelchair users, short and tall staff, pregnant staff, and people with back conditions
workstationInclusion.minimumDesk: 700–720mm fixed desk height for wheelchair access; sit-stand preferred (620–1280mm range)
workstationInclusion.clearanceUnderDesk: Knee clearance minimum 680mm H × 800mm W × 500mm D for wheelchair approach
workstationInclusion.mobilePedestals: Under-desk pedestals must be removable for wheelchair users — do not specify fixed pedestal solutions for accessible workstations
workstationInclusion.roundedCorners: Recommend rounded desk corners where possible — reduces injury risk and is more inclusive for vision-impaired staff

circulationInclusion.wheelchairPathways: Minimum 900mm clear width for wheelchair circulation; 1,200mm preferred for two-way accessible circulation
circulationInclusion.turningCircle: 1,540mm clear turning circle for powered wheelchairs at corridor junctions and beside key furniture elements
circulationInclusion.furnitureFreeZones: Reception, meeting room entrances, and bathroom approaches must maintain full accessible clearance — no furniture should encroach on these zones

sensoryInclusion.acousticConsiderations: Open plan offices can be overwhelming for neurodiverse staff — recommend acoustic pods or focus booths in any open-plan layout over 15 people
sensoryInclusion.lightingFlexibility: Where possible, position workstations to allow individuals to adjust their lighting environment — avoid locking all task lighting to building standards
sensoryInclusion.colourContrast: Furniture selection should provide visual contrast between workstations, pathways, and walls for staff with low vision

receptionAccessibility.requirement: Reception counter must include at least one section at accessible height (750–900mm max, 700mm knee clearance)
receptionAccessibility.sightlines: Reception staff must be able to see and communicate with visitors at wheelchair height — avoid counters so high they create a visual barrier
receptionAccessibility.loweredSection: Most FSZ and GOJO reception stations can be configured with a lowered section — always specify this for new fit-outs

breakoutAndSocialSpaces.tableClearance: Minimum 700mm knee clearance under all breakout tables
breakoutAndSocialSpaces.chairVariety: Breakout areas should include chairs with armrests and without — different mobility needs are met by different chair types
breakoutAndSocialSpaces.floorLevel: Avoid raised platform areas in breakout spaces — step-free access throughout
